hero.h1: Water Testing and Filtration in Geneva, IL
hero.sub: Geneva's water changed in 2008, and a lot of homes still have equipment set up for the old water. We test what comes out of your tap, tell you whether your softener is still earning its keep and install only the filtration you actually want. From our office on Campbell Street.

blocks.h2: Water Treatment Options for Geneva Homes
blocks.intro: We install, service and sometimes remove:

tiles.body: Under-sink reverse osmosis or carbon filters for the kitchen tap.
Reduce chlorine taste and smell at every faucet.
Adjust an old softener for today's water, or take it out if you no longer need it.
Testing and treatment for homes outside city water.

bodies: Geneva gets its water from deep and shallow wells. Before 2008, that water went out very hard. Since the city's reverse osmosis plant on Keslinger Road opened, about 85% of the water is treated by reverse osmosis and the finished hardness is about 5 to 7 grains. The city itself says residents may be able to reduce or eliminate water softeners.

A test at your tap shows where your water stands today. If you have a softener set up for the old hard water, it may be wasting salt and water, or you may not need it at all. We'll show you the numbers and let you decide.

blocks.intro: Geneva's water story is different from most of its neighbors.

items.body: Many homes put in softeners when the water was very hard. Those settings may be far higher than today's water needs.
In homes near downtown, rust from old galvanized supply pipe can discolor water even when the city water is clean. [Leak and pipe repair](/geneva/leak-repairs) fixes the cause.
Some homeowners still like a drinking water filter at the kitchen sink. We install under-sink systems with a separate faucet.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Do I still need a water softener in Geneva?
items.preview: Maybe not. The city's water has been softened since 2008.
items.answer: Maybe not. Since 2008, Geneva's reverse osmosis plant has brought finished hardness down to about 5 to 7 grains, and the city says residents may be able to reduce or eliminate softeners. A test at your tap tells you for sure.

items.q: Can you remove my old softener?
items.answer: Yes. We remove the softener and brine tank and reconnect the plumbing with a proper bypass or straight pipe.

items.q: Does Geneva use Fox River water?
items.preview: No. The city uses wells and reverse osmosis treatment.
items.answer: No. Geneva draws from deep and shallow wells and treats most of the water with reverse osmosis at its plant on Keslinger Road.

items.q: Do you install under-sink water filters?
items.answer: Yes. We install under-sink carbon and reverse osmosis systems with a dedicated faucet.

items.q: How much does water filtration cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the system. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the system, its size and how it connects to your plumbing. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
